messages:
Mira Patel: Heads up — after the NCCL roll this morning in eu-west we’re seeing a 20-30% tail-latency spike on multi-GPU jobs and 3 nodes with kernel oops. Affected profiles: large all-reduce and model-parallel evals.
Jonas Lee: Yikes. Is it strictly NCCL or a driver/kernel combo? Any common kernel version?
Rekha Singh: Logs point to a timing regression after kernel 6.5.x + nvidia-driver 546.x + NCCL 2.17 combination. Stack traces show repeated stalls in all-reduce and then an oops. Short snippet: `NCCL INFO all_reduce ring 0 timeout after 120s` and kernel: `BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s`
Samir Ortiz: We should freeze upgrades on affected pools and route traffic to the fallback capacity pool. Immediate actions I propose: hold packages in the image repo, label nodes so orchestration avoids them, and open a short deploy freeze for EU region.
Samir Ortiz: Commands we can run now (deb/rpm + k8s label):
```
# Debian/Ubuntu: hold packages so future apt upgrades don't bite us
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-546 nvidia-kernel-source-546 nvidia-utils-546
# RHEL/CentOS: versionlock
sudo yum versionlock add nvidia-driver-546* 
# Kubernetes: mark nodes as frozen and cordon/drain for maintenance
kubectl label node <node> infra.driver.freeze=546 --overwrite
kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Jonas Lee: Also, we should update the image-builder to pin driver/CUDA in the golden images and create a temporary apt repo snapshot for eu-west that contains only the vetted packages. Ops-bot, can you create a holdlist entry?
ops-bot: Created holdlist: repo=redwood-apt-eu-west, snapshot=2026-03-18-nccl-rollback, pinned=[nvidia-driver-546,nvidia-utils-546,cuda-12.2,nccl-2.17]. TTL: 72h.
deploy-bot: Rollback job queued: infra/driver-rollback/1795001234, will run canary on pool-gpu-fallback-1 first.
Rekha Singh: I'll prepare a conservative NCCL package that reverts the ABI bump (keep driver and kernel unchanged) — if we can avoid full driver rollback that’s lower risk. ETA ~2h.
Mira Patel: Plan for next 4 hours: 1) freeze upgrades + apt snapshot (ops) 2) cordon + drain 3 nodes with oops and replace from fallback 4) deploy rollback canary on 2 nodes in fallback pool 5) monitor perf telemetry and logs (latency + NCCL timeouts). If canary is green, expand to 20% traffic.
Jonas Lee: I'll start the billing impact estimate — moving jobs to fallback reserved capacity will increase committed utilization. Ballpark +$1.2k/day if we shift 30% of GP-hours to dedicated backup.
Rekha Singh: Also adding an immediate test matrix: A100/H100 x CUDA 12.1/12.2 x kernel 5.15/6.1/6.5 — small synthetic all-reduce and broadcast tests. I’ll push the harness and run parallel jobs.
Mira Patel: Good. After rollback we need a lockstep upgrade matrix: kernel + driver + NCCL + CUDA permutations, plus a staged canary with perf gates (p99 tail, NCCL timeout count). No single-component upgrades anymore without passing the matrix.
Samir Ortiz: I'll draft a short runbook snippet to add to incidents: how to pin packages (apt-mark/yum), how to label nodes, and how to revert to snapshot images.
Mira Patel: Can everyone ack on this plan? If yes we freeze upgrades for eu-west and start the rollback canary.
Jonas Lee: ACK :thumbsup:
Rekha Singh: ACK, starting tests now.
Samir Ortiz: ACK — holding packages and labeling nodes.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed to pool-gpu-fallback-1 (2 nodes). Monitoring hooks: nccl.timeouts, driver.oops, p99-latency.
ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1422. Added links: holdlist, rollback job, telemetry dashboard.
Mira Patel: Thanks all. After we stabilise I’ll own the postmortem and we’ll schedule the lockstep upgrade window next sprint. Keep updates in this thread only.
